featured_techniques.technique: Beloved vs. everyday company framework (cup analogy) to guide product, service, and hiring decisions
Hiring for soul and life-alignment with company mission
Zappos-like litmus test: two-month onboarding with an exit option and $2,000 payoff
Linking employee commitment to repeat business (customer experience impact)

sections.description: The speaker introduces a pledge of belief that converts a fuzzy idea into actionable practices, inviting the audience to affirm the pledge.
sections.title: Introduction: Pledge of Belief

sections.description: Bliss differentiates beloved companies, which bind the organization around serving customers’ lives, from everyday firms that merely execute tasks. She begins the cup-manufacturer example to illustrate how products and customer experiences diverge when the company focuses on life context versus simple sales.
sections.title: Beloved vs. Everyday Companies: The Cup Analogy

sections.description: Continuing the analogy, Bliss asks what it means to hire people who fit the soul of the company and how clarity of purpose defines recruitment and retention, emphasizing that alignment with serving customers’ lives guides hiring decisions.
sections.title: Cup Manufacturer Analogy: Hiring and Cultural Fit

sections.description: Bliss explains Zappos’ approach: a two-month onboarding phase where employees can leave for a $2,000 payment, a test of genuine commitment. With attrition under 2%, the company achieves approximately 75% of daily orders from repeat customers, illustrating how commitment translates into customer loyalty.
sections.title: Zappos Litmus Test: Commitment and Outcomes

summary: In this brief talk, Jeanne Bliss reframes a fuzzy notion of belief into concrete organizational practices that center on trust between employees and customers. She contrasts “beloved” companies—those that think through customers’ lives and experiences—with task-focused, “everyday” firms, using a cup-manufacturer analogy and the example of Zappos to illustrate how hiring, onboarding, and commitment can produce meaningful outcomes like high repeat business. The speech emphasizes hiring for soul and purpose, and describes a two-month onboarding litmus test at Zappos that offers a $2,000 payoff to those who leave, revealing a strong link between employee commitment and customer satisfaction.
title: Jeanne Bliss: A Pledge of Believe — Do You Believe Your Customers and Employees?
